column1: # Phase-contract migration: pinned historical inventory schema -> current
# executor phase.
# Sprint 118 / Story #4 / Story-ID 759341a95870.
# THE PROBLEM. tests/tour/inventory.tsv (frozen by docs/tour/pin.tsv,
# inventory_data_sha256) spells the compiled mode of a build-only row
# `bpp_compiled:transpile-build-run`, and its interpreted mode
# `bpp_interpreted:parse-or-run`. Both strings contain a `run` token. A
# build-only (`norun`) row must NOT have its body executed: the sprint-118
# master execution plan §5 says so, and executing it is precisely the defect
# the superseded tour-evidence/v2 runner had.
# THE DECISION. The CURRENT MASTER PLAN OUTRANKS THE STALE PINNED STRING.
# The executor implements no body execution for the four build-only rows. The
# historical inventory schema is NOT rewritten — it is pinned evidence of what
# Sprint 98 recorded, tests/tour/inventory.tsv and docs/tour/pin.tsv stay
# byte-for-byte as they are, and tools/tour/validate.sh keeps deriving its
# vocabulary from docs/tour/differential-schema.tsv unchanged.
# THIS TABLE IS THE BRIDGE, AND IT IS CHECKED AT BOTH ENDS.
# tools/tour/executor-gate.rb requires that
#   * every executable inventory row still declares exactly the
#     `historical_token` named here for its (applicability, mode) — so the
#     historical schema cannot be quietly edited to agree with the new
#     behaviour, and
#   * docs/tour/executor-contract.tsv declares exactly the `current_phase` and
#     the `executes_body` policy named here — so the new behaviour cannot be
#     quietly widened back into running a `norun` body.
# A ledger observation carries the current phase; the historical token stays
# joinable through this table. Nothing is silently reinterpreted.
# applicability
